ch27.d.sw: Charge from the battery, or discharge through the resistor with the battery out. Switching while running takes effect at that instant
ch27.goal.exp: Charging and discharging an RC circuit: charge and current change exponentially
ch27.goal.tau: One time constant $\tau = RC$ sets how fast
ch27.obs.tau: At $t = \tau$ the charge has covered 63 % of the way to its final value and the current has dropped to 37 %
ch27.obs.tangent: The tangent at the switching instant (dashed) reaches the final value at $t = \tau$
ch27.obs.i: The current starts at its maximum $\mathcal{E}/R$ and falls to 0: as the capacitor voltage approaches the emf, less voltage is left across $R$
ch27.obs.switch: Switch to discharge halfway: discharge starts from the charge at that instant and the current reverses ($i < 0$)
ch27.obs.RC: Doubling $R$ or $C$ doubles $\tau$ and stretches the curves in time by 2. Changing $C$ while running keeps the charge $q$, so $V_C = q/C$ jumps
ch27.assume: Battery emf 12 V; internal and wire resistance neglected. Moving dots show the flow of positive charge (conventional current)
